                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How do you change the port for a TanStack Start app?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-03-29, last updated: 2025-04-01, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79543987/how-do-you-change-the-port-for-a-tanstack-start-app)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since the current version of TanStack Start uses Vinxi under the hood, you can update your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`package.json`scripts to pass in the port like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Or just the CLI command:'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Migrating Tanstack Start from Vinxi to Vite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-07-24, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://blog.logrocket.com/migrating-tanstack-start-vinxi-vite/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do that, run the following commands:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm uninstall vinxi\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install vite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next, update the scripts in your `package.json` to use Vite’s standard `dev` and `build` commands:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"scripts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dev": "vite dev --port 3000",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"build": "vite build",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, because Start is now a Vite plugin, the `app.config.ts` file is redundant and should be replaced with a `vite.config.ts` file, where Start can be registered as a Vite plugin.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do this, delete the `app.config.ts` file in your project directory and add a `vite.config.ts` file with the following code:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// vite.config.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { defineConfig } from 'vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default defineConfig({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'plugins: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsconfigPaths(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// you can register other plugins e.g tailwindcss()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tanstackStart()\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How can I specify vite server options when ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-12, last updated: 2026-04-16, [Read more](https://github.com/TanStack/router/discussions/4023)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'port: Number(process.env.HMR_PORT!),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* Vinxi launches two separate HMR (Hot Module Replacement) servers—one for the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* Starting with v0.5.6, you can explicitly assign fixed HMR ports in the config.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* ⚠️ Do *not* configure both HMR ports in `viteMain`—Vinxi will try to assign the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* same port to both and throw an error.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* With fixed ports, you can write stable reverse proxy rules, such as:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* - https://example.dev/_build/client/hmr → http://localhost:4224\n'[39m +
                      [32m'* - https://example.dev/_build/server/hmr → http://localhost:4334\n'[39m +
                      [32m'*\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import type { InlineConfig } from 'vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'const vite: InlineConfig = {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"allowedHosts: ['your host here'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'plugins: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// this is the plugin that enables path aliases\n'[39m +
                      [32m'viteTsConfigPaths({\n'[39m +
                      [32m"projects: ['./tsconfig.json'],\n"[39m +
                      [32m'}),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tailwindcss(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const config = defineConfig({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsr: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"appDirectory: 'src',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'vite,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'export default config'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build a Project from Scratch | TanStack Start React Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/start/v0/docs/framework/react/build-from-scratch)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Update Configuration Files\n'[39m +
                      [32m`We'll then update our package.json to use your build tool's CLI and set "type": "module":\n`[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"build": "vite build"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Then configure TanStack Start's build tool plugin:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'vite.config.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { defineConfig } from 'vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import viteReact from '@vitejs/plugin-react'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default defineConfig({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'port: 3000,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resolve: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsconfigPaths: true,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'plugins: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tanstackStart(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m"// react's vite plugin must come after start's vite plugin\n"[39m +

                      [32m'## Port configuration\n'[39m +

                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the server does not bind to the correct port, set a [custom start command](/deployments/start-command):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PORT=$PORT node .output/server/index.mjs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Getting Started\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To run this application:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                    [32m'npm install\n'[39m +
                    [32m'npm run dev\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Building For Production\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To build this application for production:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                    [32m'npm run build\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Styling\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This project uses [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Removing Tailwind CSS\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If you prefer not to use Tailwind CSS:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'1. Remove the demo pages in `src/routes/demo/`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'2. Replace the Tailwind import in `src/styles.css` with your own styles\n'[39m +
                    [32m'3. Remove `tailwindcss()` from the plugins array in `vite.config.ts`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'4. Remove `@tailwindcss/vite` and `tailwindcss` from `package.json`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Routing\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This project uses [TanStack Router](https://tanstack.com/router) with file-based routing. Routes are managed as files in `src/routes`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Adding A Route\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To add a new route to your application just add a new file in the `./src/routes` directory.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'TanStack will automatically generate the content of the route file for you.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Now that you have two routes you can use a `Link` component to navigate between them.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Adding Links\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To use SPA (Single Page Application) navigation you will need to import the `Link` component from `@tanstack/react-router`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m'import { Link } from "@tanstack/react-router";\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Then anywhere in your JSX you can use it like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<Link to="/about">About</Link>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This will create a link that will navigate to the `/about` route.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'More information on the `Link` component can be found in the [Link documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/v1/docs/framework/react/api/router/linkComponent).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using A Layout\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'In the File Based Routing setup the layout is located in `src/routes/__root.tsx`. Anything you add to the root route will appear in all the routes. The route content will appear in the JSX where you render `{children}` in the `shellComponent`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Here is an example layout that includes a header:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { HeadContent, Scripts, createRootRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export const Route = createRootRoute({\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  head: () => ({\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    meta: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m"      { charSet: 'utf-8' },\n"[39m +
                    [32m"      { name: 'viewport', content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' },\n"[39m +
                    [32m"      { title: 'My App' },\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  shellComponent: ({ children }) => (\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <html lang="en">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <head>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <HeadContent />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      </head>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <body>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <header>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          <nav>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            <Link to="/">Home</Link>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            <Link to="/about">About</Link>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          </nav>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        </header>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {children}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <Scripts />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      </body>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </html>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'More information on layouts can be found in the [Layouts documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/routing-concepts#layouts).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Server Functions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'TanStack Start provides server functions that allow you to write server-side code that seamlessly integrates with your client components.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'const getServerTime = createServerFn({\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  method: 'GET',\n"[39m +
                    [32m'}).handler(async () => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return new Date().toISOString()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'// Use in a component\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function MyComponent() {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  const [time, setTime] = useState('')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  useEffect(() => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    getServerTime().then(setTime)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }, [])\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return <div>Server time: {time}</div>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## API Routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can create API routes by using the `server` property in your route definitions:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n"[39m +
                    [32m"import { json } from '@tanstack/react-start'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"export const Route = createFileRoute('/api/hello')({\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  server: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    handlers: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"      GET: () => json({ message: 'Hello, World!' }),\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Data Fetching\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"There are multiple ways to fetch data in your application. You can use TanStack Query to fetch data from a server. But you can also use the `loader` functionality built into TanStack Router to load the data for a route before it's rendered.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"export const Route = createFileRoute('/people')({\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  loader: async () => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    const response = await fetch('https://swapi.dev/api/people')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    return response.json()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  component: PeopleComponent,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function PeopleComponent() {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  const data = Route.useLoaderData()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <ul>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      {data.results.map((person) => (\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <li key={person.name}>{person.name}</li>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </ul>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Loaders simplify your data fetching logic dramatically. Check out more information in the [Loader documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading#loader-parameters).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Data Mutations | TanStack Router Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-05, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/router/v1/docs/guide/data-mutations)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'When mutations related to loader data are made, we can use router.invalidate to invalidate committed, cached, and in-flight loader generations.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Matching active preload lanes are retired, and selected current active matches reload through the normal loading protocol:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'const router = useRouter()\n'[39m +

                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'Current active routes reload through the normal loading protocol; cached inactive data remains marked stale and reloads when it is reused.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the error was the result of a route load, you should instead call router.invalidate(), which will coordinate both a router reload and an error boundary reset:\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Invalidating the Router Context\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to invalidate the context state you are passing into the router, you can call the invalidate method to tell the router to recompute the context.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This is useful when you need to update the context state and have the router recompute the context for all routes.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'當進行與載入器資料 (loader data) 相關的變更時，我們可以使用 router.invalidate 強制 Router 重新載入所有當前路由匹配：\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'如果您想等待所有載入器完成後再失效，請將 {sync: true} 傳入 router.invalidate：\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Hosting | TanStack Start React Docs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-01, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/start/v0/docs/framework/react/guide/hosting)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Start Deployment Targets | tanstack/router | DeepWiki\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-02-14, last updated: 2026-07-15, [Read more](https://deepwiki.com/tanstack/router/5.4-start-deployment-targets)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Deployment Flow**: The Vite build process transforms source files into deployment artifacts.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Client assets are bundled into `dist/client/` with code splitting and optimization.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Server code is bundled into `dist/server/server.js` for standard deployments or `.output/server/index.mjs` for Nitro deployments.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The deployment target determines which runtime executes the server bundle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Deployment Target|Server Runtime|Package Dependencies|Start Command|Output Location|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**srvx**|Node.js|`srvx` (via pnpx)|`pnpx srvx --prod -s ../client dist/server/server.js`|`dist/server/`, `dist/client/`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `dist/server/server.js`: The server bundle to execute\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Script|Command|Purpose|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`preview`|`vite preview`|Test production build locally before deployment|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`start`|Varies by deployment target|Run production server|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- srvx deployment: `"start": "pnpx srvx --prod -s ../client dist/server/server.js"` examples/react/start-trellaux/package.json10\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Nitro deployment: `"start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"` examples/react/start-basic/package.json10'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building and Inspecting Tanstack Start Production Builds - Grasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://paths.grasp.study/public-courses/7348a52b-431d-46f3-be49-57877ff0037d/modules/9125ba58-7f1d-47a0-b934-446a55ff08f8/lessons/d528c3b4-f8d4-4e71-9d8a-7a56d3c49bf6)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm run build` executes the `vite build` command, which bundles your application for production.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With a client-side rendered app, you might use `vite preview`, which serves the static files from the `dist` folder.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"**This is not correct for an SSR application.** The `vite preview` command only serves static files; it doesn't run your server-side logic.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'To properly run your production SSR build, you must execute the server entry point.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A conventional Tanstack Start project includes a `start` script in `package.json` for this purpose:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm start` will start a web server using your production-ready server bundle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This server will perform the full SSR process for every request, just as it would in a live production environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can then access `http://localhost:3000` (or another configured port) in your browser to see the fully-rendered application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Build Command:** `npm run build` (or `vite build`) generates a production-ready version of your application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Local Preview:** Use `npm start` (or the equivalent command to run your `dist/server` entry point) to test your production SSR build locally, not `vite preview`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# 'Cannot get /' on a TanStack Start project in vite preview mode #202\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-10-12, last updated: 2026-05-21, [Read more](https://github.com/TanStack/cli/issues/202)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m''[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Data & State Management\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/start/latest)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'One Router-first app, from server request to client navigation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start keeps TanStack Router as the application contract, then adds full-document rendering, streaming, typed server work, middleware, and output for the runtime you choose.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Routes, params, search schemas, loaders, links, pending states, and boundaries stay TanStack Router.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start adds the server and build layers around that same tree.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start supports Vite and Rsbuild and is designed for different hosting providers and runtimes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Deployment configuration changes; route authoring and server boundaries do not.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Use TanStack Start with Bun\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-28, [Read more](https://bun.com/docs/guides/ecosystem/tanstack-start)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Change to the project directory and run the dev server with Bun.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cd my-tanstack-app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'bun --bun run dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This starts the Vite dev server with Bun.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<Step title="Update scripts in package.json">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Modify the scripts field in your `package.json` by prefixing the Vite CLI commands with `bun --bun`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This ensures that Bun executes the Vite CLI for common tasks like `dev`, `build`, and `preview`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```json package.json icon="file-json" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"dracula"}}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"scripts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dev": "bun --bun vite dev", // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"build": "bun --bun vite build", // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"serve": "bun --bun vite preview" // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"start": "bun run .output/server/index.mjs" // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import path from 'node:path'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Configuration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const SERVER_PORT = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000)\n'[39m +
                      [32m"const CLIENT_DIRECTORY = './dist/client'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"const SERVER_ENTRY_POINT = './dist/server/server.js'"[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to Deploy TanStack Router to Production\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-03, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/how-to/deploy-to-production)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[[redirects]]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[build]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'publish = "dist"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'command = "npm run build"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 4.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Deploy via Git\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Connect your GitHub repository to Cloudflare Pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Set build settings: - **Build command:** npm run build\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Build output directory:** dist\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Root directory:** (leave empty)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wrangler pages publish dist --project-name=my-app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For TanStack Start (SSR) Applications\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If using TanStack Start with SSR, use this configuration instead:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"functions": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"app/server.ts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"runtime": "nodejs18.x"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"routes": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"src": "/(.*)",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dest": "/api/server"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 3.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Build Configuration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Ensure your package.json has the correct build script:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"scripts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"build": "vite build",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"preview": "vite preview"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'build: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m"outDir: 'dist',\n"[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Configured environment variables with VITE_ prefix'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build & Preview 404 - TanStack\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-10-03, last updated: 2026-03-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1423598463601479781)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'src/routes/ - Set up root.tsx following the documentation - Added server functions with createServerFn in src/server - Configured vite.config.ts as per the guide **Issue:** - `pnpm dev` works perfectly ✅ - `pnpm build` succeeds ✅ - `pnpm preview` shows "Cannot GET /" ❌ - `node dist/server/server.js` doesn\'t start (no output, port not listening) ❌ **What i tried** - Using `@netlify/vite-plugin-tanstack-start` → breaks dev mode - Using `vinxi` → errors with `dirname` in ES modules\n'[39m +
                      [32m"- Using `node dist/server/server.js` → server doesn't listen on any port **Config:** - Using file-based routing - Server functions with createServerFn - Tailwind 4 + DaisyUI **Repo** https://github.com/Smailen5/portfolio-website/tree/fix/tanstanck-build-preview Is there a way to test the production build locally?"[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# What is the difference between "vite" and "vite preview"?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-08-26, last updated: 2026-03-22, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71703933/what-is-the-difference-between-vite-and-vite-preview)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dev": "vite",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"preview": "vite preview"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`npm run dev` (or `vite`) starts a local web server with Hot Module Replacement for development, and will automatically change when code changes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`npm run build` (or `vite build`) builds the project, and outputs to the folder `./dist`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`npm run preview` (or `vite preview`) start a local web server that serves the built solution from `./dist` for previewing\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Beware\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- You need to run `build` before `preview`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `Preview` will always preview the latest build, and will not update automatically when code changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'According to the Vite documentation, vite is a command that starts a dev server in the current directory, while vite preview is a command that locally previews the production build.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In other words, vite is for developing your project with features like hot module replacement (HMR), while vite preview is for testing your project after you have built it with vite build\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Vite preview is a CLI utility that can be used to preview Vite projects in a production-like environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It builds the project, starts a production server, and opens a browser to the server URL.'[39m
                  }
                ]
              },

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building and Inspecting Tanstack Start Production Builds - Grasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://paths.grasp.study/public-courses/7348a52b-431d-46f3-be49-57877ff0037d/modules/9125ba58-7f1d-47a0-b934-446a55ff08f8/lessons/d528c3b4-f8d4-4e71-9d8a-7a56d3c49bf6)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm run build` executes the `vite build` command, which bundles your application for production.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To properly run your production SSR build, you must execute the server entry point.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A conventional Tanstack Start project includes a `start` script in `package.json` for this purpose:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm start` will start a web server using your production-ready server bundle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This server will perform the full SSR process for every request, just as it would in a live production environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can then access `http://localhost:3000` (or another configured port) in your browser to see the fully-rendered application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Build Command:** `npm run build` (or `vite build`) generates a production-ready version of your application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Local Preview:** Use `npm start` (or the equivalent command to run your `dist/server` entry point) to test your production SSR build locally, not `vite preview`.'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Deploying to a node-server - TanStack\n'[39m +

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Start Deployment | TanStack/router | DeepWiki\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-07-21, last updated: 2026-07-30, [Read more](https://deepwiki.com/TanStack/router/5.7-start-deployment)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Model|Build Output|Primary Command / Target|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**Nitro SSR**|`.output/server/index.mjs`|`node .output/server/index.mjs`docs/start/framework/react/guide/hosting.md85|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**srvx**|`dist/server/server.js`|`pnpx srvx --prod -s ../client dist/server/server.js`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To start the production server, use:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# No .output directory when building Tanstack Start for ...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-09-30, last updated: 2026-08-09, [Read more](https://node.school/blog/tanstack-start-no-output-directory/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the RC version I was using, Start’s prod build no longer bundles Nitro automatically.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You now get a dist/ with a server bundle you must run behind your own server runtime (Node HTTP, Hono, Fastify, Bun, etc.).\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'I created a\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server.mjs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file in the apps root and pasted the following:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { Hono } from 'hono'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { serve } from '@hono/node-server'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { serveStatic } from 'hono/serve-static.module'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import handler from './dist/server/server.js'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'const app = new Hono()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'serve({ fetch: app.fetch, port: Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000 })\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Then simply update the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'packages.json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'file accordingly:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"scripts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"start": "node server.mjs"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Now you should be ready to host your node application!'[39m
                  },

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations like git, npm, docker, etc. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Before executing the command, please follow these steps:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'1. Directory Verification:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use listFiles to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'   - Examples of proper quoting:\n'[39m +

            [32m'- When issuing multiple commands:\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m"- NEVER run destructive git commands (push --force, reset --hard, checkout ., restore ., clean -f, branch -D) unless the user explicitly requests these actions. Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER skip hooks (--no-verify, --no-gpg-sign, etc) unless the user explicitly requests it\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run force push to main/master, warn the user if they request it\n'[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How do you change the port for a TanStack Start app?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-03-29, last updated: 2025-04-01, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/79543987/how-do-you-change-the-port-for-a-tanstack-start-app)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Since the current version of TanStack Start uses Vinxi under the hood, you can update your\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`package.json`scripts to pass in the port like this:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Or just the CLI command:'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Migrating Tanstack Start from Vinxi to Vite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-07-24, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://blog.logrocket.com/migrating-tanstack-start-vinxi-vite/)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do that, run the following commands:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm uninstall vinxi\n'[39m +
                      [32m'npm install vite\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Next, update the scripts in your `package.json` to use Vite’s standard `dev` and `build` commands:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"scripts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dev": "vite dev --port 3000",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"build": "vite build",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'However, because Start is now a Vite plugin, the `app.config.ts` file is redundant and should be replaced with a `vite.config.ts` file, where Start can be registered as a Vite plugin.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To do this, delete the `app.config.ts` file in your project directory and add a `vite.config.ts` file with the following code:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// vite.config.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { defineConfig } from 'vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import tsconfigPaths from 'vite-tsconfig-paths'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default defineConfig({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'plugins: [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tsconfigPaths(),\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// you can register other plugins e.g tailwindcss()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'tanstackStart()\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How can I specify vite server options when ...\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Build a Project from Scratch | TanStack Start React Docs\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Update Configuration Files\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Deploy a TanStack Start App | Railway Guides\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'## Port configuration\n'[39m +
                      [32m"TanStack Start's Vinxi server listens on port 3000 by default.\n"[39m +
                      [32m"To make it respect Railway's `PORT` variable, check your `app.config.ts`:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'```typescript\n'[39m +
                      [32m'// app.config.ts\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { defineConfig } from '@tanstack/react-start/config';\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default defineConfig({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'port: Number(process.env.PORT) || 3000,\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'});\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If the server does not bind to the correct port, set a [custom start command](/deployments/start-command):\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                      [32m'PORT=$PORT node .output/server/index.mjs\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```'[39m
                  },

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# TanStack Start: Part 1 - Project Setup - SwiftAce\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-03-27, last updated: 2026-05-14, [Read more](https://swiftace.org/posts/tanstack-start-part-1)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To configure Vite, create a file `vite.config.ts` in the project root with the following code:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import { defineConfig } from 'vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'import { nitro } from "nitro/vite"\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import viteReact from '@vitejs/plugin-react'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'export default defineConfig({\n'[39m +
                      [32m'plugins: [tanstackStart(), nitro(), viteReact()],\n'[39m +
                      [32m'server: { port: 3000 }, // listen for requests on port 3000\n'[39m +
                      [32m'resolve: { tsconfigPaths: true }, // use import "paths" from tsconfig.json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'})\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `@tanstack/react-start` configures Vite to handle HTTP requests using TanStack Start, enabling routing, server-side rendering, response streaming, server functions, etc.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"The setting `server.port: 3000` configures Vite to use the network port 3000^[12]^ for the development server, and `resolve.tsConfigPaths: true` instructs Vite to resolve imports e.g. `import { X } from '@/utils'` according to the `tsconfig.json` file defined earlier^[13]^."[39m
                  },

                  content: [32m'Welcome to your new TanStack Start app!\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Getting Started\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To run this application:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                    [32m'npm install\n'[39m +
                    [32m'npm run dev\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Building For Production\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To build this application for production:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```bash\n'[39m +
                    [32m'npm run build\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Styling\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This project uses [Tailwind CSS](https://tailwindcss.com/) for styling.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Removing Tailwind CSS\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'If you prefer not to use Tailwind CSS:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'1. Remove the demo pages in `src/routes/demo/`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'2. Replace the Tailwind import in `src/styles.css` with your own styles\n'[39m +
                    [32m'3. Remove `tailwindcss()` from the plugins array in `vite.config.ts`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'4. Remove `@tailwindcss/vite` and `tailwindcss` from `package.json`\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Routing\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This project uses [TanStack Router](https://tanstack.com/router) with file-based routing. Routes are managed as files in `src/routes`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Adding A Route\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To add a new route to your application just add a new file in the `./src/routes` directory.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'TanStack will automatically generate the content of the route file for you.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Now that you have two routes you can use a `Link` component to navigate between them.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Adding Links\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'To use SPA (Single Page Application) navigation you will need to import the `Link` component from `@tanstack/react-router`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m'import { Link } from "@tanstack/react-router";\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Then anywhere in your JSX you can use it like so:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m'<Link to="/about">About</Link>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'This will create a link that will navigate to the `/about` route.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'More information on the `Link` component can be found in the [Link documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/v1/docs/framework/react/api/router/linkComponent).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'### Using A Layout\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'In the File Based Routing setup the layout is located in `src/routes/__root.tsx`. Anything you add to the root route will appear in all the routes. The route content will appear in the JSX where you render `{children}` in the `shellComponent`.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Here is an example layout that includes a header:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { HeadContent, Scripts, createRootRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'export const Route = createRootRoute({\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  head: () => ({\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    meta: [\n'[39m +
                    [32m"      { charSet: 'utf-8' },\n"[39m +
                    [32m"      { name: 'viewport', content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' },\n"[39m +
                    [32m"      { title: 'My App' },\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    ],\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  shellComponent: ({ children }) => (\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <html lang="en">\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <head>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <HeadContent />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      </head>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      <body>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <header>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          <nav>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            <Link to="/">Home</Link>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'            <Link to="/about">About</Link>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'          </nav>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        </header>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        {children}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <Scripts />\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      </body>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </html>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  ),\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'More information on layouts can be found in the [Layouts documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/routing-concepts#layouts).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Server Functions\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'TanStack Start provides server functions that allow you to write server-side code that seamlessly integrates with your client components.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'const getServerTime = createServerFn({\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  method: 'GET',\n"[39m +
                    [32m'}).handler(async () => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return new Date().toISOString()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'// Use in a component\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function MyComponent() {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"  const [time, setTime] = useState('')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  useEffect(() => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    getServerTime().then(setTime)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  }, [])\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  \n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return <div>Server time: {time}</div>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## API Routes\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'You can create API routes by using the `server` property in your route definitions:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n"[39m +
                    [32m"import { json } from '@tanstack/react-start'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"export const Route = createFileRoute('/api/hello')({\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  server: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    handlers: {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"      GET: () => json({ message: 'Hello, World!' }),\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'## Data Fetching\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"There are multiple ways to fetch data in your application. You can use TanStack Query to fetch data from a server. But you can also use the `loader` functionality built into TanStack Router to load the data for a route before it's rendered.\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'For example:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```tsx\n'[39m +
                    [32m"import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router'\n"[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m"export const Route = createFileRoute('/people')({\n"[39m +
                    [32m'  loader: async () => {\n'[39m +
                    [32m"    const response = await fetch('https://swapi.dev/api/people')\n"[39m +
                    [32m'    return response.json()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  },\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  component: PeopleComponent,\n'[39m +
                    [32m'})\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'function PeopleComponent() {\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  const data = Route.useLoaderData()\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  return (\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    <ul>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      {data.results.map((person) => (\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        <li key={person.name}>{person.name}</li>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'      ))}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    </ul>\n'[39m +
                    [32m'  )\n'[39m +
                    [32m'}\n'[39m +
                    [32m'```\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'Loaders simplify your data fetching logic dramatically. Check out more information in the [Loader documentation](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading#loader-parameters).\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'# Demo files\n'[39m +

                      [32m'When mutations related to loader data are made, we can use router.invalidate to invalidate committed, cached, and in-flight loader generations.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'### Invalidating the Router Context\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to invalidate the context state you are passing into the router, you can call the invalidate method to tell the router to recompute the context.\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'所有當前路由匹配的失效過程會在背景執行，因此現有資料將持續提供服務，直到新資料準備就緒，就像您導航至新路由一樣。\n'[39m +
                      [32m'如果您想等待所有載入器完成後再失效，請將 {sync: true} 傳入 router.invalidate：\n'[39m +

                      [32m'const router = useRouter()\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const addTodo = async (todo: Todo) => {\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                  [32m'        <div className="pointer-events-none absolute -left-20 -top-24 h-56 w-56 rounded-full bg-[radial-gradient(circle,rgba(79,184,178,0.32),transparent_66%)]" />\n'[39m +
                  [32m'        <div className="pointer-events-none absolute -bottom-20 -right-20 h-56 w-56 rounded-full bg-[radial-gradient(circle,rgba(47,106,74,0.18),transparent_66%)]" />\n'[39m +

                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Start Deployment Targets | tanstack/router | DeepWiki\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2026-02-14, last updated: 2026-07-15, [Read more](https://deepwiki.com/tanstack/router/5.4-start-deployment-targets)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'**Deployment Flow**: The Vite build process transforms source files into deployment artifacts.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Client assets are bundled into `dist/client/` with code splitting and optimization.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Server code is bundled into `dist/server/server.js` for standard deployments or `.output/server/index.mjs` for Nitro deployments.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The deployment target determines which runtime executes the server bundle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Deployment Target|Server Runtime|Package Dependencies|Start Command|Output Location|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|**srvx**|Node.js|`srvx` (via pnpx)|`pnpx srvx --prod -s ../client dist/server/server.js`|`dist/server/`, `dist/client/`|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `dist/server/server.js`: The server bundle to execute\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|Script|Command|Purpose|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`preview`|`vite preview`|Test production build locally before deployment|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'|`start`|Varies by deployment target|Run production server|\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- srvx deployment: `"start": "pnpx srvx --prod -s ../client dist/server/server.js"` examples/react/start-trellaux/package.json10\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- Nitro deployment: `"start": "node .output/server/index.mjs"` examples/react/start-basic/package.json10'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building and Inspecting Tanstack Start Production Builds - Grasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://paths.grasp.study/public-courses/7348a52b-431d-46f3-be49-57877ff0037d/modules/9125ba58-7f1d-47a0-b934-446a55ff08f8/lessons/d528c3b4-f8d4-4e71-9d8a-7a56d3c49bf6)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm run build` executes the `vite build` command, which bundles your application for production.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'With a client-side rendered app, you might use `vite preview`, which serves the static files from the `dist` folder.\n'[39m +
                      [32m"**This is not correct for an SSR application.** The `vite preview` command only serves static files; it doesn't run your server-side logic.\n"[39m +
                      [32m'To properly run your production SSR build, you must execute the server entry point.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A conventional Tanstack Start project includes a `start` script in `package.json` for this purpose:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm start` will start a web server using your production-ready server bundle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This server will perform the full SSR process for every request, just as it would in a live production environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can then access `http://localhost:3000` (or another configured port) in your browser to see the fully-rendered application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Build Command:** `npm run build` (or `vite build`) generates a production-ready version of your application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Local Preview:** Use `npm start` (or the equivalent command to run your `dist/server` entry point) to test your production SSR build locally, not `vite preview`.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m"# 'Cannot get /' on a TanStack Start project in vite preview mode #202\n"[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-10-12, last updated: 2026-05-21, [Read more](https://github.com/TanStack/cli/issues/202)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m''[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Data & State Management\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-10, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/start/latest)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'One Router-first app, from server request to client navigation.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start keeps TanStack Router as the application contract, then adds full-document rendering, streaming, typed server work, middleware, and output for the runtime you choose.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Routes, params, search schemas, loaders, links, pending states, and boundaries stay TanStack Router.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start adds the server and build layers around that same tree.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Start supports Vite and Rsbuild and is designed for different hosting providers and runtimes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Deployment configuration changes; route authoring and server boundaries do not.'[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Use TanStack Start with Bun\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-28, [Read more](https://bun.com/docs/guides/ecosystem/tanstack-start)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Change to the project directory and run the dev server with Bun.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'cd my-tanstack-app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'bun --bun run dev\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This starts the Vite dev server with Bun.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'<Step title="Update scripts in package.json">\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Modify the scripts field in your `package.json` by prefixing the Vite CLI commands with `bun --bun`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This ensures that Bun executes the Vite CLI for common tasks like `dev`, `build`, and `preview`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```json package.json icon="file-json" theme={"theme":{"light":"github-light","dark":"dracula"}}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"scripts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dev": "bun --bun vite dev", // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"build": "bun --bun vite build", // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"serve": "bun --bun vite preview" // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"start": "bun run .output/server/index.mjs" // [!code ++]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"import path from 'node:path'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'// Configuration\n'[39m +
                      [32m'const SERVER_PORT = Number(process.env.PORT ?? 3000)\n'[39m +
                      [32m"const CLIENT_DIRECTORY = './dist/client'\n"[39m +
                      [32m"const SERVER_ENTRY_POINT = './dist/server/server.js'"[39m
                  },
                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to Deploy TanStack Router to Production\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-08-03, [Read more](https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/how-to/deploy-to-production)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[[redirects]]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'[build]\n'[39m +
                      [32m'publish = "dist"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'command = "npm run build"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 4.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Deploy via Git\n'[39m +
                      [32m'1. Connect your GitHub repository to Cloudflare Pages\n'[39m +
                      [32m'2. Set build settings: - **Build command:** npm run build\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Build output directory:** dist\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Root directory:** (leave empty)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'wrangler pages publish dist --project-name=my-app\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### 2.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'For TanStack Start (SSR) Applications\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If using TanStack Start with SSR, use this configuration instead:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'json\n'[39m +
                      [32m'```\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"functions": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"app/server.ts": {\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"runtime": "nodejs18.x"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m'},\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"routes": [\n'[39m +
                      [32m'{\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"src": "/(.*)",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dest": "/api/server"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +
                      [32m']\n'[39m +
                      [32m'}\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# What is the difference between "vite" and "vite preview"?\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-08-26, last updated: 2026-03-22, [Read more](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/71703933/what-is-the-difference-between-vite-and-vite-preview)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"dev": "vite",\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'"preview": "vite preview"\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`npm run dev` (or `vite`) starts a local web server with Hot Module Replacement for development, and will automatically change when code changes\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`npm run build` (or `vite build`) builds the project, and outputs to the folder `./dist`\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`npm run preview` (or `vite preview`) start a local web server that serves the built solution from `./dist` for previewing\n'[39m +
                      [32m'### Beware\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- You need to run `build` before `preview`.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- `Preview` will always preview the latest build, and will not update automatically when code changes.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'According to the Vite documentation, vite is a command that starts a dev server in the current directory, while vite preview is a command that locally previews the production build.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In other words, vite is for developing your project with features like hot module replacement (HMR), while vite preview is for testing your project after you have built it with vite build\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Vite preview is a CLI utility that can be used to preview Vite projects in a production-like environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'It builds the project, starts a production server, and opens a browser to the server URL.'[39m
                  }

                  {
                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Building and Inspecting Tanstack Start Production Builds - Grasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: undefined, last updated: 2026-07-24, [Read more](https://paths.grasp.study/public-courses/7348a52b-431d-46f3-be49-57877ff0037d/modules/9125ba58-7f1d-47a0-b934-446a55ff08f8/lessons/d528c3b4-f8d4-4e71-9d8a-7a56d3c49bf6)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm run build` executes the `vite build` command, which bundles your application for production.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'To properly run your production SSR build, you must execute the server entry point.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'A conventional Tanstack Start project includes a `start` script in `package.json` for this purpose:\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Running `npm start` will start a web server using your production-ready server bundle.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This server will perform the full SSR process for every request, just as it would in a live production environment.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You can then access `http://localhost:3000` (or another configured port) in your browser to see the fully-rendered application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Build Command:** `npm run build` (or `vite build`) generates a production-ready version of your application.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'- **Local Preview:** Use `npm start` (or the equivalent command to run your `dist/server` entry point) to test your production SSR build locally, not `vite preview`.'[39m
                  },

                    text: [32m'# No .output directory when building Tanstack Start for ...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'In the RC version I was using, Start’s prod build no longer bundles Nitro automatically.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'You now get a dist/ with a server bundle you must run behind your own server runtime (Node HTTP, Hono, Fastify, Bun, etc.).\n'[39m +

                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

                      [32m'```\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of questions this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "where is the authentication logic implemented"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "find all usages of the config parser"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how does the ignore-walk module work"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### guide\n'[39m +
            [32m"A comprehensive guide for learning about Pochi's capabilities, features, and configuration.\n"[39m +
            [32m'This agent helps users understand how to use Pochi effectively, fetch documentation, and modify their config file (.pochi/config.jsonc) with proper confirmation.\n'[39m +
            [32m"**IMPORTANT: Any request to modify Pochi's configuration must be handled by this agent.**\n"[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Trigger examples:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- General info: "what can Pochi do?", "what agents/tools are available?", "how does Pochi work?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### planner\n'[39m +
            [32m'Engage this agent to formulate comprehensive, technical implementation strategies for feature development, system refactoring, or defect resolution.\n'[39m +
            [32m'This agent is strictly limited to planning and architectural design; it DOES NOT execute code modifications.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "create a plan to implement the user authentication feature"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "how should we refactor the database schema"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- "design a solution for the memory leak issue"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Always include a reminder in your prompt to ensure the result will be submitted through the `attemptCompletion` tool.\n'[39m +

            [32m'When NOT to use the newTask tool:\n'[39m +

            [32m'3. Each agent invocation is stateless. You will not be able to send additional messages to the agent, nor will the agent be able to communicate with you outside of its final report.
